newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle slow at $67 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle slow at $67 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Friday sold at $67.00 per cwt in light volume, unchanged from Thursday, but down $1.00 from most of this week's trade Monday through Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
An estimated 800 head of steers sold near midday in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area. There were no reported sales in Kansas on Friday.

Prices next week were seen likely at $67.00, with packer bids expected at $66.00 and owners pricing cattle at $67.00 to $68.00, they said. Packers reportedly were well stocked with cattle following active sales the last two weeks.

Texas Panhandle cattle feeders had their hands full with weathering an unusual spring storm overnight and early Friday, which dumped heavy rain and wet snow. The moisture turned feedlots muddy and made conditions miserable for cattle and cowboys, managers said.
Weight gains were expected to be thrown off by the weather before warmer, drier weather moves in Sunday which should give pens and cattle a chance to dry out and recover, they said.
The wet weather was seen boosting pasture conditions, resulting in "great" grazing this spring, said C.C. Burgess, president of the Texas and Southwest Cattle Raisers Association.
